steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Cards lift slightly to group offers.

steps.question: Which shape roles does it need?

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs and raised cards in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.22:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So customers see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for Aster's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. A modest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve twice the 4px control corner. So a plan card reads as one object without feeling soft, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and each brand colors a neutral base (brand.q1).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
steps.pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line, 1.23:1 on surface.raised, beside the light shadow that does most of the lift. So customers see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line, 1.41:1 on surface.raised (#334155, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So customers see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur at 16%, four times the card's blur. So a menu floats clear above the cards in every brand, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still floats above the cards, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships for every brand (theming.values).
